key_insight: A reinforcement-learning controller enabled autonomous fixed-wing interception of maneuvering targets in real flight.
engineering_relevance: Vision-based neural control could extend autonomous interception beyond the short range and limited endurance of quadcopter platforms.
method: Map filtered monocular vision observations directly to actuator commands with a neural network.
Train the policy using proximal policy optimization in a custom Python simulation environment.
Compare against two classical guidance controllers in simulation and validate on a fixed-wing aircraft.
evidence_signal: The policy outperformed classical controllers under most simulated conditions and successfully intercepted maneuvering fixed-wing targets in real flight.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify success rates or establish robustness across broader weather, visibility, and target conditions.
paper_title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning
